main_body: 4x3 grid of riveted steel floor/wall panels (plain, hatch, split plate, light panel) separated by dark seams; a terrain patch, not a standing object
top_band: none as a standing object; column x=47 shows a repeating 8-row panel pattern (dark seam, lighter 1-row edge L=118, then mid-tone L=70 face), i.e. tiling plate bevels, not a 3/4 top
evidence: The kind is terrain (a tiling surface patch), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. There are no receding side faces and no object top/front split to fail. Panels carry bevelled highlight edges and inset hatches, which suits a floor or wall autotile block.

style.evidence: Measured: 8 distinct colours, 6 per tile, 0% flat-fill coverage, 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The paving reference has 7 per tile and 7 colours, so the candidate is at or above it, but it is well below the grass reference (26 per tile, 80 colours). Seams and outlines are a tinted dark blue-slate, not neutral black. Shading has about 5 steps (dark seam, deep, mid, light, highlight rivets), plus bevel highlights, rivets, hatches and light accents on the panels, so no large area is a flat fill. It is simpler than the grass reference but comparable to the paving reference, so it is acceptable beside it.
